lines.text: Which lands first? A geology hammer, or a falcon feather?
lines.phonemes: wˌɪtʃ lˈændz fˈɜːst? ɐ dʒɪˈɑːlədʒi hˈæmɚ, ɔːɹ ɐ fˈælkən fˈɛðɚ?

lines.text: On Earth, it's no contest. From shoulder height, the hammer lands in about half a second. The feather? Still drifting down.
lines.phonemes: ˌɔn ˈɜːθ, ɪts nˈoʊ kˈɑːntɛst. fɹʌm ʃˈoʊldɚ hˈaɪt, ðə hˈæmɚ lˈændz ɪn ɐbˌaʊt hˈæf ɐ sˈɛkənd. ðə fˈɛðɚ? stˈɪl dɹˈɪftɪŋ dˈaʊn.

lines.text: Now take the air away. On the Moon, in nineteen seventy-one, astronaut David Scott dropped both. They landed together. "Mister Galileo was correct in his findings," he said.
lines.phonemes: nˈaʊ tˈeɪk ðɪ ˈɛɹ ɐwˈeɪ. ɔnðə mˈuːn, ɪn nˈaɪntiːn sˈɛvəntiwˌʌn, ˈæstɹənˌɔːt dˈeɪvɪd skˈɑːt dɹˈɑːpt bˈoʊθ. ðeɪ lˈændᵻd təɡˈɛðɚ. "mˈɪstɚ ɡˌælɪlˈeɪoʊ wʌz kɚɹˈɛkt ɪn hɪz fˈaɪndɪŋz," hiː sˈɛd.

lines.text: For nearly two thousand years, most scholars followed Aristotle: heavier things fall faster. Gravity does pull the hammer harder. But a heavier thing is harder to speed up, by exactly as much. So without air, they tie.
lines.phonemes: fɔːɹ nˌɪɹli tˈuː θˈaʊzənd jˈɪɹz, mˈoʊst skˈɑːlɚz fˈɑːloʊd ˈæɹɪstˌɑːtəl : hˈɛviɚ θˈɪŋz fˈɔːl fˈæstɚ. ɡɹˈævᵻɾi dˈʌz pˈʊl ðə hˈæmɚ hˈɑːɹdɚ. bˌʌt ɐ hˈɛviɚ θˈɪŋ ɪz hˈɑːɹdɚ tə spˈiːd ˈʌp, baɪ ɛɡzˈæktli æz mˈʌtʃ. sˌoʊ wɪðˌaʊt ˈɛɹ, ðeɪ tˈaɪ.

lines.text: How exact is exactly? Starting in twenty sixteen, a satellite let two metals fall around Earth for months. They matched to within a few parts in a million billion.
lines.phonemes: hˌaʊ ɛɡzˈækt ɪz ɛɡzˈæktli? stˈɑːɹɾɪŋ ɪn twˈɛnti sˈɪkstiːn, ɐ sˈæɾəlˌaɪt lˈɛt tˈuː mˈɛɾəlz fˈɔːl ɚɹˈaʊnd ˈɜːθ fɔːɹ mˈʌnθs. ðeɪ mˈætʃt tʊ wɪðˌɪn ɐ fjˈuː pˈɑːɹts ɪn ɐ mˈɪliən bˈɪliən.

lines.text: Measure it: on the Moon, that drop takes about one point four seconds. On Earth, under six tenths.
lines.phonemes: mˈɛʒɚɹ ɪt: ɔnðə mˈuːn, ðæt dɹˈɑːp tˈeɪks ɐbˌaʊt wˈʌn pˈɔɪnt fˈɔːɹ sˈɛkəndz. ˌɔn ˈɜːθ, ˌʌndɚ sˈɪks tˈɛnθs.

lines.text: Gravity speeds them up equally. Only the air tells them apart.
lines.phonemes: ɡɹˈævᵻɾi spˈiːdz ðˌɛm ˌʌp ˈiːkwəli. ˈoʊnli ðɪ ˈɛɹ tˈɛlz ðˌɛm ɐpˈɑːɹt.

lines.text: Next: a spinning office chair. Pull in your arms, and it spins faster. Why?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: ɐ spˈɪnɪŋ ˈɑːfɪs tʃˈɛɹ. pˈʊl ɪn jʊɹ ˈɑːɹmz, ænd ɪt spˈɪnz fˈæstɚ. wˈaɪ?
